proximal_convergence.summary: Verified natural molecular cases converge on modulation or disruption of anthocyanin-pathway flux, but not on one universal gene.

examples.Ipomoea purpurea: naturally occurring albino/pale variants implicate CHS loss-of-function and bHLH regulatory variation
examples.Parrya nudicaulis: natural purple-white polymorphism implicates petal-specific CHS downregulation / cis-regulatory control
examples.Pleione limprichtii: natural rose-purple/pink/white populations implicate FLS, ANS, UFGT and MBW-network expression

important_counterexamples_or_bounds: Abronia fragrans is a natural white/pink system involving betalain rather than anthocyanin pigmentation.
Boechera stricta provides strong natural ecological and plasticity evidence but not a resolved proximal molecular white-state mechanism.
Digitalis purpurea, Medicago sativa and Vicia faba candidate papers do not satisfy the strict natural-population molecular-evidence boundary used here.
interpretation: The evidence supports recurrent proximal convergence on reducing or rerouting pigment-pathway output in several natural anthocyanic systems.
It does not support a single universal white-flower gene.
It does not establish nonwhite-to-white evolutionary direction.
It does not establish pollinator or temperature causation.
